items.text: Optional, install railing around the front porch and handrails on one side of the stairs. Porch is 29 inches, under the 30 inch rule, so only if the inspector calls it.
items.priceBasis: Est. 240 min at $35.71/hr ($250 per 7-hour day) = $143. Set posts and rail around roughly 20 ft of porch edge plus a handrail on the steps, anchored into concrete. Material left blank — depends on the railing you spec.

items.text: Front porch steps, resurface the crumbling concrete or replace the step. Trip hazard. Resurfacing may only last about a year; a new step lasts 10 to 15.
items.priceBasis: Est. 150 min at $35.71/hr ($250 per 7-hour day) = $90. Break out loose concrete, bond and resurface the crumbling step. Material left blank: depends on resurface vs. new step.

items.text: Front porch, tighten the metal railing so it does not move.
items.priceBasis: Est. 30 min at $35.71/hr ($250 per 7-hour day) = $18. Re-anchor the loose railing base into the porch concrete. Material is masonry anchors.

items.text: Exterior right, clear all the weeds touching the house.
items.priceBasis: Est. 45 min at $35.71/hr ($250 per 7-hour day) = $27. Pull and cut weeds along the right foundation and walkway edge.

items.text: Exterior right, clean up the fence line. Clear it about five feet up.
items.priceBasis: Carried from the earlier SOW, where this was two lines ($54 brush cleanup + $36 clearing five feet up). Est. 150 min at $35.71/hr ($250 per 7-hour day) = $90.

items.text: Exterior rear, clear away the debris: the tire, the gasoline can, and the rake.
items.priceBasis: Est. 15 min at $35.71/hr ($250 per 7-hour day) = $9. Pick up three items and carry them to the curb.

items.text: Exterior rear, cut the grass, clean the fence line about five feet up, and make sure no branches or trees hang five feet or lower.
items.priceBasis: Est. 180 min at $35.71/hr ($250 per 7-hour day) = $108. Mow the full rear yard, clear the fence line, and cut overhanging branches down to five feet.

items.text: Exterior left, clear away any weeds and trees touching the left side of the house.
items.priceBasis: Est. 60 min at $35.71/hr ($250 per 7-hour day) = $36. Cut the growth pressed against the left wall back off the siding.

items.text: Clear away the weeds on the driveway.
items.priceBasis: Est. 45 min at $35.71/hr ($250 per 7-hour day) = $27. Pull and scrape weeds out of the full run of concrete joints.

items.text: Exterior front, cut away any trees or weeds touching the siding.
items.priceBasis: Est. 20 min at $35.71/hr ($250 per 7-hour day) = $12. Pull the weed clump and small tree at the bay window foundation.

items.text: Exterior rear, repair the broken siding. This spot plus three or four other cracked spots.
items.priceBasis: Est. 120 min at $35.71/hr ($250 per 7-hour day) = $72. About 25 min each for 4-5 cracked spots. Material left blank: depends on matching the siding.

items.text: Exterior rear, remove the cable wires and patch the holes they leave in the siding.
items.priceBasis: Est. 45 min at $35.71/hr ($250 per 7-hour day) = $27. Pull the dead cable runs off the meter wall and seal the screw and wire holes. Material is exterior sealant.

items.text: Exterior rear, put a patch over the dryer vent hole or install a proper dryer vent.
items.priceBasis: Est. 30 min at $35.71/hr ($250 per 7-hour day) = $18. Cover the vent hole with a patch plate. Material left blank: patch vs. a new dryer vent.

items.text: Optional, repair the driveway tripping hazards and the dip in the driveway.
items.priceBasis: Est. 180 min at $35.71/hr ($250 per 7-hour day) = $108. Patch the worst broken slabs and fill the dip. Material left blank: depends how much concrete you want to do.

items.text: Install five 10-year sealed smoke detectors, one in each bedroom, one in the basement, one in the hallway. The current battery detectors will not pass Section 8.
items.priceBasis: Est. 75 min at $35.71/hr ($250 per 7-hour day) = $45. Five detectors at about 15 min each including ladder work. Material is 5 sealed 10-year detectors at about $25.

items.text: Basement stairs, extend the handrail two feet at the top so it covers the top two stairs.
items.priceBasis: Est. 45 min at $35.71/hr ($250 per 7-hour day) = $27. Add brackets and a 2 ft extension at the top of the stair rail. Material left blank: rail length and brackets.

items.text: Basement, replace the light fixture to make it functional.
items.priceBasis: Est. 25 min at $35.71/hr ($250 per 7-hour day) = $15. Swap the lampholder on the existing box and test. Material is the lampholder and bulb.

items.text: Basement, install a blank cover on the open junction box to prevent exposed wires.
items.priceBasis: Est. 10 min at $35.71/hr ($250 per 7-hour day) = $6. Tuck the wire nuts back in and screw on a blank cover. Matches a past job at $6/$10.

items.text: Basement, board up the bathroom wall and the wiring to the left of the bathroom door so the wires and the switch box are not exposed.
items.priceBasis: Est. 90 min at $35.71/hr ($250 per 7-hour day) = $54. Cut and fasten sheet goods over the open stud bay beside the bathroom door, cut around the switch box. Material is roughly one sheet.

items.text: Basement, drywall around the electrical panel and fill the hole in the bathroom wall.
items.priceBasis: Est. 180 min at $35.71/hr ($250 per 7-hour day) = $108. Frame and hang drywall around the panel area, cut around the panel, fill the bathroom wall hole, tape and first coat. Material left blank: sheet count unknown.

items.text: Basement bathroom, drywall the ceiling.
items.priceBasis: Est. 240 min at $35.71/hr ($250 per 7-hour day) = $143. Hang and tape drywall on a small bathroom ceiling, about 5x7 ft. Material left blank: sheet count unknown.

items.text: Basement bathroom, screw the door shut so it cannot be opened, and caulk the wall next to the bathroom.
items.priceBasis: Est. 30 min at $35.71/hr ($250 per 7-hour day) = $18. Screw the door to the frame and run a caulk bead along the wall. Material is screws and caulk.

items.text: Basement bathroom, make sure the two old drain openings in the floor by the left wall are sealed.
items.priceBasis: Est. 15 min at $35.71/hr ($250 per 7-hour day) = $9. Check both plugs are tight and seal if needed.

items.text: Remove the loose cable wire throughout the basement.
Basement, remove the screws and nails from the board or hammer them flat. Cut hazard.
items.priceBasis: Est. 15 min at $35.71/hr ($250 per 7-hour day) = $9. Pull or flatten the protruding fasteners on the one board.

items.text: Basement, stabilize the laundry sink legs so they sit firmly under the sink and it does not move.
items.priceBasis: Est. 30 min at $35.71/hr ($250 per 7-hour day) = $18. Reset the legs under the basin and anchor it so it stops moving.

items.text: Remove the random loose hanging wires above the laundry sink.
items.priceBasis: Est. 25 min at $35.71/hr ($250 per 7-hour day) = $15. Cut out the dead wiring in the joist bay above the sink.

items.text: Basement, install a floor drain cover.
items.priceBasis: Est. 10 min at $35.71/hr ($250 per 7-hour day) = $6. Set a drop-in cover in the floor drain. Material is the cover.

items.text: Basement, repair the crack in the drywall at the bottom of the stairs. Skim coat, sand down, and repaint.
items.priceBasis: Est. 90 min at $35.71/hr ($250 per 7-hour day) = $54. Scrape, skim coat, sand and repaint the cracked corner. On-site time only. Material is compound and paint.

items.text: Dining room, tighten the outlet under the window.
items.priceBasis: Est. 10 min at $35.71/hr ($250 per 7-hour day) = $6. Pull the plate, tighten the device in the box, refit.

items.text: Kitchen, replace the ripped window screen above the sink.
items.priceBasis: Est. 30 min at $35.71/hr ($250 per 7-hour day) = $18. Pull the sash screen and fit the replacement.

items.text: Kitchen, remove the old smoke detector bracket from the ceiling.
items.priceBasis: Est. 15 min at $35.71/hr ($250 per 7-hour day) = $9. Unscrew the bracket, fill the two screw holes, touch up paint.

items.text: Kitchen, repair or replace the GFCI outlet to the right of the fridge. It does not work and will not reset. Fix the wiring as needed.
items.priceBasis: Est. 45 min at $35.71/hr ($250 per 7-hour day) = $27. Check the wiring, swap the GFCI outlet, test. Material is the GFCI.

items.text: Cut the spray foam sealing the rear window shut and make the window open.
items.priceBasis: Est. 45 min at $35.71/hr ($250 per 7-hour day) = $27. Cut the foam out of the sash gaps and free the window so it opens.

items.text: Bathroom, repair the hole near the shower curtain rod.
items.priceBasis: Est. 30 min at $35.71/hr ($250 per 7-hour day) = $18. Patch the hole around the rod bracket, re-set the bracket. Material is patch compound.

items.text: Install a rod for clothes in the closet.
items.priceBasis: Est. 30 min at $35.71/hr ($250 per 7-hour day) = $18. Mount rod sockets and cut a rod to the closet width. Material is rod and sockets.

items.text: Make the outlet next to the rear window flush to the wall and tighten the cover plate. Replace the outlet if needed.
items.priceBasis: Est. 20 min at $35.71/hr ($250 per 7-hour day) = $12. Shim the outlet flush with spacers and tighten the plate. Material is outlet spacers.

items.text: Make the door latch and open smoothly.
items.priceBasis: Est. 30 min at $35.71/hr ($250 per 7-hour day) = $18. Adjust the strike plate and hinges so the door latches and swings freely.

questions.text: Did I put the keys back?
